## Deep Thought {.center}

> The agent builds you something amazing in five minutes, then the 10% that's wrong takes longer to fix than the 90% that was right took to build. But it never feels that way. It always feels like you're right on the precipice of completion.

**[help! my husband is addicted to Claude Code.](https://hils.substack.com/p/help-my-husband-is-addicted-to-claude)** — Hilary Gridley (writerbuilder)

Why it's here: the "almost done" feeling is a gamification trick, not a status report. Worth noticing when *you* feel it mid-workshop.

🗳️ **Engage:** [TODO: reaction mechanism -- e.g. vote yes/no on "I've felt this"]

## Deep Thought {.center}

> Folks often assume what they lack are skills, when they often lack skills AND well-refined ideas.

**[The prototyping bottleneck](https://www.frank.computer/blog/2026/03/prototyping-bottleneck.html)** — frank.computer

Includes a "prototype slop zone" diagram worth looking at directly.

Why it's here: AI removes the skills bottleneck faster than it removes the "do I actually have a good idea" bottleneck.

🗳️ **Engage:** [TODO: reaction mechanism -- e.g. poll "which bottleneck do you hit more often: skills or ideas?"]

## Deep Thought {.center}

> Control quality and relevance with your own behavior more than with "heaps of extraneous detail."

**[Code is the byproduct](https://yagmin.com/blog/code-is-the-byproduct/)** — yagmin.com

Why it's here: a counterpoint to the instinct to write ever-longer prompts/AGENTS.md files instead of steering as you go.

🗳️ **Engage:** [TODO: reaction mechanism -- e.g. comment thread "one habit I use to steer AI output"]

## Deep Thought {.center}

> Sometimes I want "do this for me," sometimes "do this with me" or "show me how."

**[The task isn't the job](https://sunilpai.dev/posts/the-task-isnt-the-job/)** — Sunil Pai

Why it's here: naming which of these three modes you actually want, before you prompt, avoids a lot of friction.

🗳️ **Engage:** [TODO: reaction mechanism -- e.g. vote on which mode you reach for most]

## Deep Thought {.center}

> If it hurts, do it more often.

**[FrequencyReducesDifficulty](https://martinfowler.com/bliki/FrequencyReducesDifficulty.html)** — Martin Fowler

Why it's here: applies as much to running tests/reviews with an agent in the loop as it did to deployments and integration.
